title: Claude Opus 5.5 Just Solved Motion Graphics (No More AI Slop)
creator: Bart Slodyczka
summary: Demo and walkthrough of a free Claude Code skill (motion-broll, repo Barty-Bart/motion-graphics) that turns a talking-head clip plus a timestamped transcript into motion-graphic b-roll timed to speech. The signature look is a single continuous shape that keeps morphing between forms instead of separate elements popping in. The repo README adds a deterministic render engine, motion blur via sub-frame blending, and an approval gate on the clip plan before any build.
what_is_shown: Side-by-side original vs. augmented ~30s talking-head clip; full-frame cutaways and side-third transparent panels in which one shape morphs pill -> card -> terminal -> chart, with a cursor driving transitions; outputs browsed in a local HTML viewer.
stack: ffmpeg (ProRes 4444 for alpha panels, MP4 cutaways)

techniques.name: Single morphing container
techniques.how: Each clip is one continuous object that changes size, radius and content through a sequence of forms rather than cutting between discrete graphics.
techniques.quality_lever: Continuity of form reads as designed motion and avoids the disjointed slide-deck look typical of AI output.

techniques.name: Pure time-function frames
techniques.how: Every frame is computed only from its timestamp; springs are closed-form step responses and CSS transitions/timers are banned.
techniques.quality_lever: Any frame can be rendered or inspected in isolation, making headless capture deterministic and debuggable.

techniques.name: Sub-frame motion blur
techniques.how: Headless Chromium captures 4 sub-frames per output frame across a 180-degree shutter and ffmpeg blends them.
techniques.quality_lever: Adds filmic motion blur that makes fast morphs feel smooth rather than strobing.

techniques.name: Speech-synced beat timing
techniques.how: Word timings are estimated from the SRT transcript and animations are keyed to the rhythm of spoken words.
techniques.quality_lever: Graphics land on emphasis words, which is what makes b-roll feel edited rather than overlaid.

techniques.name: Plan-then-approve clip list
techniques.how: Before building, the skill lists each clip with on-screen text, type (full cutaway, side-third panel, or none) and position for user approval; density presets (medium ~3, heavy 4-5 clips).
techniques.quality_lever: Cheap human gate catches bad editorial choices before expensive renders.

techniques.name: Data honesty placeholders
techniques.how: Never invents figures; bars show only relative size and text uses skeleton lines until real numbers are supplied.
techniques.quality_lever: Prevents hallucinated stats from shipping inside polished graphics.

techniques.name: Layout-aware cutaways
techniques.how: Footage inspection determines resolution, fps and picture-in-picture layout so panels sit in the third of frame away from the speaker's face.
techniques.quality_lever: Graphics respect the existing composition instead of covering the subject.

prompting_patterns: Paste the repo URL and ask Claude to read and import the skill into the workspace (it can also create CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md).
Invoke /motion-broll with video + SRT, choose density and palette, and explicitly ask for results embedded in a local HTML page for review.
Supply brand colors/style resources on first use instead of relying on the default palette.
pipeline: inspect footage (res/fps/layout) -> estimate word timings from SRT -> plan clips (cutaway/panel/none) -> user approval -> build each clip + still checks -> render with motion blur -> preview render, compare.html, viewer.html, TIMING.md -> final assembly in user's own editor
pitfalls: Skill cannot transcribe; a timestamped transcript must be provided (suggested ElevenLabs API or a local model).
Opening frame of output was weak.
Earlier versions of the skill looked noticeably worse; quality depends on accumulated skill resources.
Default palette will not match a brand without customization.
Generation took roughly 15 minutes for ~30s of footage; preview render is review-only.
evidence: oEmbed title/channel; watch-page description (bot-protected, partial); transcript via youtubetotranscript.com (read as model summary); repo README at github.com/Barty-Bart/motion-graphics; aitoolsreview.co.uk page for duration. SKILL.md body itself not visible.

title: Opus 5.5 Makes Insane Videos. Here's the Full Workflow
creator: Lukas Margerie
summary: A survey-style workflow for code-generated launch/product videos with Opus 5.5, arguing the surrounding harness matters far more than the prompt. Covers rendering routes, a pasted set of 'motion studio rules', brand grounding, reference-video style extraction, markdown memory specs with a beat grid, code-synthesized sound synced to BPM, long director's briefs, and a scored self-critique loop, ending with packaging it all as a reusable skill.
what_is_shown: 15-20s showreels and product launch films (MagicPath), weather-forecast test animation, reference-styled launch video, narrated product explainer, and cited community examples (Steve Jobs story video synced at 120 BPM, multi-hour director-brief films).

techniques.name: Four rendering routes
techniques.how: Model chooses between hand-coded frames captured headless, a video framework (Remotion/HyperFrames/Diffusion Studio), a hybrid with image/video models composited by Opus, or editing existing footage.
techniques.quality_lever: Naming the route up front avoids the zero-dependency default when a framework would give more control.

techniques.name: Motion studio rules file
techniques.how: Project-level instructions in four parts: render contract, a 'look' section banning generic output (centered text, gradients), sound guidance, and a feedback-loop stage.
techniques.quality_lever: Encodes taste and render reliability once so every prompt inherits it.

techniques.name: Reference grammar extraction
techniques.how: Download a reference video, pull frames at intervals, write a style guide (palette, type, shot lengths, transitions, camera moves, grain, text entry/exit), then a shot list in that style.
techniques.quality_lever: Borrows craft vocabulary from proven work while explicitly forbidding copying content, logos or characters.

techniques.name: Markdown memory specs + beat grid
techniques.how: Claude writes style, brand, tone and UI-component spec files plus a gotchas list and a frame-level beat-grid table reviewed before coding.
techniques.quality_lever: Consistency across scenes and a reviewable timing blueprint before expensive builds.

techniques.name: Never-cut container direction
techniques.how: 'Product film UI motion' brief: one container that morphs size, radius and fill while content swaps behind a short blur.
techniques.quality_lever: Same continuity principle as Slodyczka's skill; gives premium, Apple-like flow.

techniques.name: Code-synthesized sound on a beats file
techniques.how: Synthesize a 120 BPM track, measure it into a beats file (beats, downbeats, hits), synthesize UI sounds in Node, then retime animation to the beats.
techniques.quality_lever: Locks visual hits to audio; creator found benefit uncertain.

techniques.name: Director's brief
techniques.how: Roughly 12-part brief: logline, references, tools/APIs, character bible, beat sheet, on-screen text, workflow gates, critique loop, deliverables; model cast as director, animator, sound designer and render engineer.
techniques.quality_lever: Output quality rose noticeably as prompt structure increased.

techniques.name: Scored critique loop
techniques.how: Model reviews its render against criteria, scores each, fixes low scores and repeats until a threshold (about 7-8/10).
techniques.quality_lever: Machine gate replaces some human review; cited example ran 163 calls over ~7 hours.

techniques.name: Self-gathered brand assets
techniques.how: Prompt has Claude research and collect screenshots and logos for a named brand itself.
techniques.quality_lever: Real brand material breaks the model's default black-and-orange house style.

prompting_patterns: One-line showreel prompt framing the model as the subject, sized to 15s (6-8 shots), with an 'go all out' style effort multiplier.
Template prompts with brand-name placeholders for automated asset research.
Explicit instruction: copy the reference's grammar, never its content.
Role stacking: director + animator + sound designer + render engineer.
Final step: package the workflow as a skill with inputs (URL, duration, format) and hard rules.
pipeline: brief + references -> (optional) brand asset gathering -> style/brand/tone/component markdown specs + gotchas -> beat grid review -> code build -> render (headless or framework) -> voiceover/sound -> scored critique loop -> package as skill
pitfalls: Generic template output (centered text, gradients) without references or brand context.
Claude Code hand-codes by default unless a framework is named or installed.
Model has a repetitive default palette (black/orange) when unconstrained.
Short unstructured prompts yield weaker results.
Copying reference content instead of style.
Polished results can take many hours and many calls.
evidence: oEmbed; watch-page description with chapter list; transcript via youtubetotranscript.com (read as model summary). Rule file itself sits in a paid kit and an X article, not read.

title: Claude Opus 5.5 Changed Motion Graphics Forever (Insane Results)
creator: Tao Prompts
summary: Broad tour of what Claude can produce in motion graphics: editorial graphics over talking heads, HUD overlays on AI video, 2D explainers, AI music videos, voxel 3D, and Blender cinematics via MCP. The recurring method is a project folder holding source footage plus a style reference, a custom skill, and external image models for assets Claude cannot render photorealistically, then many feedback rounds.
what_is_shown: Split-screen editorial graphics with subtitles over talking head; Iron Man style head-tracking HUD; 2D sci-fi explainer; lyric music video in brushstroke style; voxel showreel and galaxy-to-atom zoom; Blender 3D cinematic scenes.
stack: GPT image model / OpenArt for assets

techniques.name: Local transcription for timing
techniques.how: Install Whisper so Claude produces an SRT with timestamps; allow Hugging Face domains in capabilities so it can download the model.
techniques.quality_lever: Timestamped script is the sync backbone for graphics against voiceover.

techniques.name: Style reference video in project folder
techniques.how: Place a reference clip beside the footage and instruct Claude to match its style.
techniques.quality_lever: References produce much better output than none even though Claude never copies them exactly.

techniques.name: External asset sheets
techniques.how: Have Claude write an image prompt for an asset sheet in the reference style, generate at 2K+ with an image model, and drop assets/logos/portraits into a reference folder.
techniques.quality_lever: Offloads photorealism Claude is weak at while Claude handles animation.

techniques.name: Sketch-over correction
techniques.how: When Claude got HUD perspective backwards, the creator drew the intended angle on a frame and fed it back.
techniques.quality_lever: Rough visual markup communicates spatial intent better than prose.

techniques.name: Preview-before-render gate
techniques.how: Claude shows a preview; stop it and give palette/design feedback before the full render.
techniques.quality_lever: Avoids wasting long renders on wrong art direction.

techniques.name: Repo-as-harness
techniques.how: Point Claude at open repos (e.g. PDoomVideo: p5.brush frames in studio.html, headless Chrome, ffmpeg, storyboard + animation guide for parallel subagents) and let it handle setup.
techniques.quality_lever: Reuses proven render pipelines and storyboard/subagent structure.

techniques.name: Blender via MCP
techniques.how: Connect Blender MCP add-on, upscale 2D assets, convert to 3D, let Claude write Blender Python and operate Blender; render overnight.
techniques.quality_lever: Extends code-driven motion into real 3D cinematics.

prompting_patterns: Voice-chat instructions: transcribe, remove awkward pauses, match reference style.
Ask Claude to author the image-generation prompt for asset sheets in the reference style.
Ask Claude for concept, lyrics and character-sheet prompts for music videos before animating.
pipeline: footage + style reference in folder -> Whisper SRT -> skill-driven first draft -> generate external assets -> iterate (subtitles, layout, variety) -> preview gate -> render; for 3D: assets -> upscale -> 2D-to-3D -> Blender MCP -> overnight render
pitfalls: First draft cut speech early, felt rushed, visuals too simple, little transition variety, no subtitles.
Claude weak at photorealistic rendering.
HUD perspective came out reversed.
Music video first draft lacked effects, lyrics, environments and props.
Low-quality 2D inputs give low-quality 3D models.
3D issues: overlapping buildings, unrealistic rocket physics, weak explosions.
First draft took ~30 minutes.
evidence: oEmbed; watch-page description (links, partial); transcript via youtubetotranscript.com (read as model summary); README of github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo. The creator's skill (Drive link truncated) was not read.

title: I Fully Automated My Video Editing Using Claude Code (Full Walkthrough)
creator: Christian Peverelli
summary: Shows a Claude Code 'editing team' where Claude orchestrates transcription, HyperFrames animation, browser research for b-roll, Tella cuts via MCP, Epidemic Sound audio and ffmpeg finishing. The core idea is a large, growing style skill that Claude rewrites after every feedback round so mistakes do not recur.
what_is_shown: A YouTube video edited overnight: cuts, zooms, layout changes, HyperFrames 4K animations, screenshot/scroll b-roll of sources, music and sound effects; 2:46 raw clip cut to 31s.

techniques.name: Agent-as-editor with tool roles
techniques.how: Claude coordinates specialised tools: transcriber, animator, researcher, screen editor, sound designer, finisher.
techniques.quality_lever: Each tool does what it is best at while Claude holds the edit plan.

techniques.name: Self-updating style skill
techniques.how: After every review round, instruct Claude to write what it learned into the skill (grew to ~1,400 lines, 36 rules).
techniques.quality_lever: Compounding taste; same errors stop recurring.

techniques.name: Small-piece calibration
techniques.how: Teach the style on short segments like the hook first, testing 8-10 sound effect options.
techniques.quality_lever: Cheap iterations to pin taste before full runs.

techniques.name: Timestamped feedback
techniques.how: Give notes tied to exact timestamps (add suspense music here, zoom when I say zoom).
techniques.quality_lever: Precise, actionable revisions instead of vague requests.

techniques.name: Verifiable research b-roll
techniques.how: Claude captures screenshots, scrolling recordings and highlighted zooms of real sources and shows only verifiable facts.
techniques.quality_lever: Grounded, credible b-roll.

techniques.name: ffmpeg QA pass
techniques.how: ffmpeg joins segments, strips black frames and checks audio sync before human review.
techniques.quality_lever: Machine gate catches technical defects.

prompting_patterns: Ask Claude Code to build the editing system and walk you through setup, then save the setup as a skill and test in a new thread.
Event-triggered instructions keyed to speech (zoom on 'zoom', SFX on mention, showcase three strongest animations).
'Learn from this session and update the skill' at the end of each round.
pipeline: record (Tella) -> raw footage to project -> Parakeet transcript -> Claude cuts/plans -> HyperFrames animations + browser b-roll -> Epidemic Sound music/SFX -> ffmpeg join/QA -> human timestamped notes -> skill update
pitfalls: Early output too busy; needed simplifying.
Palettes and sound choices off-taste until corrected.
SFX require trial and error.
Feedback not saved to the skill means repeated errors.
Tools need logins/connectors before use; human review still needed.
evidence: oEmbed; watch-page description; transcript via youtubetotranscript.com (read as model summary). Skill itself (Skool community) not read.

title: Claude Opus 5.5 + JavaScript = INSANE 2D Animations (Full Tutorial)
creator: RandomAI
summary: Three-level tutorial for 2D narrative animation with Opus 5.5 in plain JavaScript: a one-line prompt, a structured prompt with style reference and pacing, and an orchestrated pipeline with MCP tools for voice, music and clips plus a HyperFrames or Remotion harness. Note the oEmbed title differs slightly from the page title.
what_is_shown: Black hole animation, hand-drawn style baby-deer story with Python-composed music, paper-collage comedy short with generated narration on a HyperFrames timeline; community examples.

techniques.name: Prompt maturity levels
techniques.how: Escalate from a one-line ask to a structured prompt (style, pacing, creative direction, story outline) to a multi-tool orchestrated pipeline.
techniques.quality_lever: Structure and references are what turn inconsistent one-shots into reliable results.

techniques.name: Code-composed soundtrack
techniques.how: Ask Opus to compose original background music in Python alongside the JS animation.
techniques.quality_lever: Royalty-free, length-matched audio without external services.

techniques.name: Iterate-until-match instruction
techniques.how: Tell the model to keep iterating until quality matches the reference style.
techniques.quality_lever: Built-in self-critique against a concrete target.

techniques.name: Harness for timeline control
techniques.how: Install HyperFrames or Remotion so scenes appear on an editable timeline and audio can be placed.
techniques.quality_lever: More control and editability than raw headless capture.

prompting_patterns: Reference video plus structured prompt covering style, pacing, direction and story outline.
Supply pacing research and a plan; the model cannot reliably invent these alone.
pipeline: idea + reference -> structured prompt + pacing plan -> JS animation -> HyperFrames/Remotion render -> Python or MCP music/voice -> timeline assembly
pitfalls: Simple prompts give inconsistent, sometimes poor results.
Structured-but-unnarrated output felt flat, cartoonish and strictly 2D.
Sonnet gives less polished animation than Opus.
evidence: oEmbed; watch-page metadata (duration, date, short description); transcript via youtubetotranscript.com (read as model summary). No companion repo or write-up found.
